notes: Home. Same frame as r2pol-052 ('The X doesn't work in the <room>'); shared construction cluster (verifier VR-11). Default: affirmative, although a fault report is more typical.

partner_turns.D: The heating suddenly kicked in.
partner_turns.Xa: Not a new heating issue, is it?
partner_turns.Xb: Alas, the heating job didn't pan out.
partner_turns.Xc: No sign of heating work done.
partner_turns.Q: Is this your spare heating?

B.source: We didn't book the table for Saturday.

notes: Restaurants/social. Default: affirmative or a suggestion ('Let's book a table').

partner_turns.Xa: Not on Saturday, we didn't book a table.
partner_turns.Xb: Our book table for Saturday fell through.
partner_turns.Xc: No trace of a reservation for Saturday.
partner_turns.Q: Are you available this Saturday?

partner_turns.Xa: Not all my family eats meat.
partner_turns.Xb: Our family dinner plans fell through.
partner_turns.Xc: No one else in your family eats meat, you've mentioned.
partner_turns.Q: Do you eat meat with your family?

B.source: The bank didn't charge me a fee for the transfer.

partner_turns.Xc: No sign of any transfer.
partner_turns.Q: Did you initiate the transfer?

partner_turns.Xb: Your Thursday ID appointment slipped our minds.
partner_turns.Xc: No one brought your ID on Thursday.
partner_turns.Q: Must bring ID on Thursday?

partner_turns.D: I've already moved the plants outside.
partner_turns.Xa: Not tonight, we can't put plants outside.
partner_turns.Xc: No plants have been moved outside yet.

A.source: My knee hurts on the stairs.

B.source: My knee doesn't hurt on the stairs.

partner_turns.Xb: Your pain didn't let up on the stairs, did it?

partner_turns.Q: Does your knee hurt on stairs?

B.source: The chicken curry doesn't have dairy in it.

notes: Food/allergy; safety-relevant. Default: affirmative or a question.

partner_turns.D: I've added chicken to the curry, but I'm not sure about the dairy.
partner_turns.Xa: No, chicken curry doesn't contain dairy.

A.source: I don't agree with the budget plan.

B.source: I agree with the budget plan.

notes: Work/meetings; dissent is the minority reading that must survive. Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.Xa: Not agreed on the budget yet.
partner_turns.Xc: No budget increase was approved.
partner_turns.Q: Is this the agreed plan?

A.source: I told the night nurse I wasn't in pain.

B.source: I told the night nurse I was in pain.

notes: Negation only in the embedded clause; main clause affirmative. Codebook counts negation of what the main clause directly embeds as negated. Health; safety-relevant. Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: I've noticed you've been restless all night.
partner_turns.Xa: Not a trace of new visitors last night.
partner_turns.Xc: No sign of pain last night.
partner_turns.Q: Is nurse aware of your discomfort tonight?

A.source: The doctor said the knee scan was clear.

B.source: The doctor said the knee scan wasn't clear.

notes: Embedded negation under a reporting verb. No agent chip: reporter (doctor) vs embedded subject (scan) is contestable, so agent is unscored. Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: The scan showed your knee is clear.
partner_turns.Xa: Not the clear scan you were hoping for, huh?
partner_turns.Xc: No sign of improvement yet.
partner_turns.Q: Is your knee scan clear?

A.source: I don't have any cash for the parking meter.

B.source: I have some cash for the parking meter.

notes: Negative-polarity item: A takes 'any', B takes 'some' (function words forced by polarity; not content words). Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: I see your parking meter has cash.
partner_turns.Xa: Not paying with cash, I see.
partner_turns.Xb: Payment declined, parking's not going through.
partner_turns.Xc: No sign of a parking meter here.
partner_turns.Q: Got cash for the meter?

A.source: My partner is coming to the dinner too.

B.source: My partner isn't coming to the dinner either.

notes: Polarity-sensitive additive: 'too' vs NPI 'either'. Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: I've just arrived for dinner.
partner_turns.Xa: Not coming for dinner tonight.
partner_turns.Xc: No one's come for dinner yet.
partner_turns.Q: Are you expecting your partner for dinner?

A.source: Nobody called about the flat viewing.

B.source: Somebody called about the flat viewing.

notes: Negative quantifier subject (nobody) instead of 'not'. No agent chip (nobody/somebody: doer unnamed). Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: I just saw a flat on the call.
partner_turns.Xa: Not viewing the call flat.
partner_turns.Xc: I've seen no sign of a call flat.
partner_turns.Q: Are you viewing the call flat?

A.source: Isn't the museum free on Sundays?

B.source: Is the museum free on Sundays?

notes: Negative yes/no question (positively biased, but negated on the words, which is what the codebook labels). Speech act question in both. Default: affirmative question.

partner_turns.D: Museums are free on Sundays.
partner_turns.Xa: Not all museums are free on Sundays.
partner_turns.Xb: Unfortunately, the free museum entry on Sundays fell through.
partner_turns.Xc: No trace of free entry on Sundays.
partner_turns.Q: Is it free on Sundays?

A.source: I drive at night in winter.

B.source: I never drive at night in winter.

notes: Frequency negator 'never' on a habitual. Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: It's slippery out tonight.
partner_turns.Xa: Not a snowy night, was it?
partner_turns.Xb: Our drive last night was cancelled.
partner_turns.Xc: No tracks to be seen.
partner_turns.Q: Was driving in the snow last night?

A.source: I don't have to wait in the hotel lobby.

B.source: I have to wait in the hotel lobby.

notes: Negated obligation ('don't have to' = no obligation, not prohibition). Speaker subject chosen to avoid the CB-1 directive reading of 'You have to'. Default: affirmative.

partner_turns.D: I've been waiting in the lobby for a while.
partner_turns.Xa: No one's joined us in the lobby yet.
partner_turns.Xb: Our earlier hotel booking didn't pan out.
partner_turns.Xc: No one new has entered the lobby.
partner_turns.Q: Is this the hotel lobby?

A.source: Leave the garden gate open.

B.source: Never leave the garden gate open.

notes: Prohibition with 'never' instead of 'don't'. Default: affirmative imperative.

partner_turns.D: I left the garden gate open.
partner_turns.Xa: You didn't leave the gate open.
partner_turns.Xc: No sign of the gate being left open.
partner_turns.Q: Did gate remain open?
